issues.description: validate_conda substring match on --version output admits impostor binaries
issues.detail: `any(tool in out.decode().lower() for tool in ['micromamba','mamba','conda'])` accepts any binary whose --version output contains those substrings (e.g. 'anaconda-project', paths like /opt/anaconda/bin/foo). Match the first token of stdout or check the executable basename instead of doing a lowercase substring scan.

issues.description: filters='*.exe' breaks the file picker on macOS and Linux
issues.detail: Conda, mamba, and micromamba are extensionless binaries on POSIX systems, so the dialog shows nothing by default for non-Windows users. Make the filter platform-conditional on sys.platform or drop it entirely; validate_conda already enforces correctness.

issues.description: validate_conda returns True for an empty string, conflating 'unset' with 'valid'
issues.detail: Returning True for '' means callers cannot trust that True implies a usable executable. Separate emptiness from validity: either split the predicate (is_empty vs is_valid) or treat empty as a precondition violation handled at the call site, so the postcondition matches the function name.

issues.description: kernelspec argv() uses the custom conda_path without re-validating it at use time
issues.detail: When custom_conda is set and find_conda fails, the stored conda_path is passed downstream without re-running validate_conda. The path may be stale, deleted, no longer executable, or never validated if it was persisted before this feature. Re-check on use and surface a precise error pointing at the preference.

issues.description: Redundant custom_conda boolean duplicates state already carried by conda_path
issues.detail: The 'custom_conda' flag and the 'conda_path' string encode the same decision twice, inviting drift between them. Treat a non-empty conda_path as the override (one value, one identity) and remove the boolean, simplifying the argv() fallback chain into a flat lookup.

issues.description: setFocus() added to shared create_browsefile/select_file helper changes behavior for every other caller
issues.detail: create_browsefile is generic widget infrastructure used across preference pages. Unconditionally calling edit.setFocus() after select_file alters focus behavior for every existing browsefile in Spyder to serve one new field. Make it opt-in via a parameter or move the call to the conda caller.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges strongly: the feature is small and well-scoped, but the validator and its file picker are sloppy. All six reviewers flagged the substring match in validate_conda as admitting impostor binaries, and all six flagged the Windows-only '*.exe' filter as breaking macOS/Linux users. Five flagged the empty-string-equals-valid conflation, and two raised that the kernelspec fallback consumes the persisted path without re-validation. Secondary concerns include the redundant custom_conda boolean alongside conda_path and a setFocus side effect smuggled into a shared widget helper. No P0 blockers; tighten the validator contract, fix the platform filter, and route the override through a single source of truth before merging.
